sentences.text:
James Daniel vs Babu Mathai on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125429329/
2 (Dated this the 7th day of August 2025)
The appellants are the petitioners in O.P.(M.V.) No.1699 of 2015 on the files of the MACT, Pathanamthitta.

The petition was filed seeking compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for the death of one Thresiamma James @ Kuttiamma, who is the wife of 1st appellant and mother of appellant Nos.2 and 3.
2.

On 25.8.2015 at about 5 a.m., while the deceased was travelling in a car bearing car registration No.KL.05.AK.144 through Perumbavoor - Aluva M.C. road in north to south direction and when the car reached INTUC Union office junction, a goods vehicle bearing registration No.KL.37/A.2531 coming from the opposite direction hit against the car and thereby, Kuttiamma sustained serious injuries.
Immediately, she was taken to Taluk head quarters hospital, Perumbavoor and on the 2025:KER:60319 way, she succumbed to the injuries.
Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are the owner and insurer of the said car, 4th respondent is the driver of the goods vehicle and respondent Nos.5 and 6 are the owner and insurer of the goods vehicle.
The appellant claimed 25,00,000/- as compensation.
3. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 remained ex parte and the 3rd respondent filed a written statement contending that the accident happened due to the negligence of the driver of the goods vehicle.

It was admitted that the car was insured with the 3rd respondent as on the date of accident but the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
4. Respondent Nos.4 and 5 together filed written statement contending that the accident happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the car.
The 6th respondent is the insurer of the goods vehicle and there was coverage at the time of accident.
The 6th respondent filed a separate a written statement supporting the contentions of respondent Nos.4 and 5 that the accident happened due to the negligence of the driver of the car.
The insurance policy of the goods vehicle at the time of accident is admitted.
The Tribunal, on the basis of Ext.Nos.A1 to A9, awarded a compensation of 11,10,000/- with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
Aggrieved by the award of compensation, this appeal is filed.
5. Counsel for the appellants submitted that the deceased was aged 46 and was a cattle rearer and sweeper earning an amount of 15,000/- per month.
The Tribunal, taking note of the fact that she was not a permanent employee and since the income is not proved, fixed the monthly income as 7,500/-.

Relying on the Supreme Court's decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 2025:KER:60319 236], the counsel for the appellants contended even for a coolie who died in an accident in 2015, a notional monthly income of 10,000/- should be applied.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 2025:KER:60319 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any evidence for monthly income, relying on Ramachandrappa (supra) the monthly income of the appellant is fixed as 10,000/-.
Since the deceased was aged 46 years, 25% of income is to be added for future prospects.
Towards personal and living expenses 1/3rd is to be deducted as the dependents are 3.
Therefore, the monthly income of the deceased can be taken as 8,333/-(10,000+25%-1/3).
The proper multiplier to be adopted as per the decision reported in Sarla Verma (Smt) and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another [(2009) 6 SCC 121], is 13.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt) and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another [(2009) 6 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the compensation for loss of dependency is calculated James Daniel vs Babu Mathai on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125429329/
3 as 8333x12x13 = 12,99,948/-.
6.

The tribunal awarded 40,000/- to the 1st appellant under loss of consortium and 25,000/-
each to appellant Nos.2 and 3 under the head of love and affection.

As per the dictum laid 2025:KER:60319 down in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and Others (2018 KHC 6697) and National Insurance Co.Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017(4) KLT 662 (SC)],
the spouse as well as children are entitled to 40,000/- each, plus 10% in every three years under loss of consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and Others (2018 KHC 6697)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017(4) KLT 662 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, appellants are entitled to 40,000/- each, plus 10% escalation in every three years, (1st increment in 31.10.2020 and 2nd increment in 31.10.2023), which totally comes to Rs.1,45,200/- (40,000 x 3 +10% +10%).

When loss of consortium is awarded, 50,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal under loss of love and affection is set aside.

7. The counsel appearing for the appellants also argued that under the head of funeral expenses and loss of estate, they are entitled to increment for every 3 years on the basis of decision reported in Pranay Sethi (supra).

Therefore, under heads of loss 2025:KER:60319 of funeral expenses and loss of estate, with 10% escalation in every three years, which will come to 18,150/- each,
(15,000+10%+10%), is awarded.

Accordingly, the following enhancements/deductions are made to the Award:
Sl. Head of Claim Amt. Awarded Amt. revised in No. by Tribunal appeal (Rs.) (Rs.) 1 Loss of dependency 9,75,000 12,99,948 2 Loss of estate 15,000 18,150 3 Funeral expenses 15,000 18,150 3. Loss of love and affection 50,000 -- 5.

In the result, the appeal is allowed, and the appellants are entitled to an amount of Rs.3,86,448/-
(Rupees three lakh eighty 2025:KER:60319 six thousand four hundred and forty eight only).
The Insurance Company shall pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum for the enhanced amounts from the date of petition till realisation.
All other findings entered by the Tribunal stand confirmed.
If any amounts have already been paid, the same shall be granted set off.

The claimants shall produce the details of the Bank account before the Insurance Company/Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment, and amount shall be transferred to the Bank account directly through NEFT/RTGS mode, within a period of one month thereafter.
If the Bank account is not furnished within the time stipulated, it is made clear that no interest shall run on the enhanced amount after the period specified by this Court.

Sd/-
BASANT BALAJI, JUDGE dl/
